'''Isztar Zawadzki''' (February 9, 1939 - February 11, 2023) was a Canadian meteorologist, born in Poland and raised in Argentina. Professor at the [[McGill Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences]] department in [[Montreal]], [[Québec]], he specialized in [[radar meteorology]], a field where he has made important contributions.

==Biography==
Zawadzki was born in [[Warsaw]], Poland on February 9, 1939, just before the outbreak of [[World War II]]. Fleeing [[anti-Semitism]] and war, his mother took refuge with him in the [[USSR]], then in Argentina.<ref name=Obit>{{cite web |language=fr |url=https://bulletin.scmo.ca/avis-de-deces-du-professeur-emerite-isztar-zawadzki-1939-2023/ |title=Avis de décès du professeur émérite Isztar Zawadzki (1939 – 2023) |author1=Jacques Derome |author2=Frédéric Fabry |author3=Henry Leighton |author4=Man K. (Peter) Yau |date=April 9, 2023 |publisher=[[Canadian Meteorological and Oceanographic Society|CMOS]] |access-date=2023-06-11}}</ref> It was in this country that he received a degree in physics from the [[University of Buenos Aires]] in 1963.<ref name=Obit/><ref name="bio1">{{cite web | language = en | url= http://www.crahi.upc.edu/imprints/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=100&catid=40&Itemid=18&lang=en | publisher= IMproving Preparedness and RIsk maNagemenT for flash floods and debriS flow events | title= Prof. Isztar Zawadzki |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170912012004/http://www.crahi.upc.edu/imprints/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=100&catid=40&Itemid=18&lang=en |archive-date=2017-09-12 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He then specialized in radar meteorology by completing a master's degree (M.Sc. 1968) and a doctorate (PhD. 1972) at [[McGill University]] in Montreal.<ref name=Obit/><ref name="bio1"/>

After his studies, he was first a professor at the [[Université du Québec à Montréal]] (UQÀM) during the 1970s where he became director of studies in atmospheric sciences from 1971 to 1982, then director of the physics department. from 1988 to 1992.<ref name="bio1"/> He then became a professor at McGill University until the end of the 2000s.<ref name="bio2">{{cite web |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160508062544/http://lassonde.yorku.ca/articles/nowcasting-precipitation-dr-zawadzki |archive-date=2016-05-08 | language = en | url= http://lassonde.yorku.ca/articles/nowcasting-precipitation-dr-zawadzki | title= Nowcasting of Precipitation with Dr. Zawadzki | publisher= [[York University]] |access-date=April 23, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> At this university, he served as the director of the [[J. S. Marshall Radar Observatory]], where he supervised several students who published important papers.

Zawadzki retired in 2010 but continued to serve as professor emeritus.<ref name="bio3">{{cite web | url= https://www.mcgill.ca/meteo/facultystaff/zawadzki | title=Prof. Isztar Zawadzki | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220928140342/https://www.mcgill.ca/meteo/facultystaff/zawadzki |archive-date=September 28, 2022 |publisher= McGill University | access-date=February 22, 2023|url-status=dead}}.</ref> He specializes in weather radar, cloud physics and nowcasting.<ref name="bio3"/> He died at age 84 on February 11, 2023, after suffering a second [[cerebrovascular accident]] (CVA).<ref name=avis-deces>{{cite web |language=fr |url=https://www.dignitymemorial.com/fr-ca/obituaries/montreal-qc/ifztar-zawadzki-11149815 |title=Isztar Zawadzki 9 février 1939 – 11 février 2023 |work=Avis de décès |year=2023 |publisher=SCI Shared Resources |access-date=2023-02-20}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Isztar Zawadzki is the author or co-author of more than 117 articles covering a wide range of applications of [[weather radar]] data and [[cloud physics]], including improving understanding of the formation processes and distribution of precipitation during winter and summer such as the growth of drops, icing of snowflakes, etc...<ref name=Obit/>

At the national and international level, Zawadzki was director of the Cooperative Research Center in Mesometeorology (McGill-UQAM-MSC) and senior scientist of the Canadian Meteorological Research Program ([[Environment and Climate Change Canada]]).<ref name="bio1"/> Doctor Zawadzki received:<ref name=Obit/><ref name="bio1"/><ref name=avis-deces/>
*1991, [[Patterson Medal]] for outstanding contribution to meteorology in Canada,
*1998 Canadian Meteorological and Oceanographic Society President's Award,
*2001, ''Fellow'' of the [[Canadian Meteorological and Oceanographic Society]],
*2004, ''Fellow'' of the [[American Meteorological Society]] (AMS),
*2007, Remote Sensing Prize of the AMS,
*2007, member of the [[Royal Society of Canada]].
